# White-Label Branding and Semantic Terminology (v1.7.0 → v1.7.5)

Planning document, drafted 2026-08-27 with 1.6.5 in production. Ports LOTTO's
self-service branding (`~/Repos/lotto/docs/CONFIGURABLE_BRANDING_PLAN.md`,
shipped in LOTTO v1.20.0) and ZEV Prism's semantic terminology system
(`~/Repos/zev_app/zev_dashboard/docs/semantic-settings.md`) into FEED.

**Implementation status, 2026-08-29 (`v1.7.5-beta.4`):** Phases 0–5 are
implemented. The database-backed wizard, runtime stylesheet, asset derivatives,
portable backup/restore, outgoing email/report identity, terminology layer, and
OKLCH migration all landed. The phase version labels below preserve the review
boundaries from the plan; they are not separate released builds.

The earlier version of this note claimed completion while two gates were still
unmet, which is worth recording because a plan that overstates its own status is
worse than one that admits a gap. Both are now closed:

- **Rendered under a non-default brand.** A real export — three procurement
  cards, actual data, a configured brand — carries every derived colour to
  paper, measured: organization name and card titles at 7.05:1 on white, meta
  text at 6.90:1, chart series at ~5:1, and a card border that tracks the
  brand's neutral harmonisation rather than a fixed grey.
- **Capstone on the deployment floor.** The appearance was driven end to end on
  an iPad mini 4 running iPadOS 15.4, which found three defects that no desktop
  browser would have: the runtime stylesheet's `oklch()` lightness form, polar
  `color-mix()` hue rotation, and the absent View Transitions API.

One finding from that PDF verification is **not** closed and is slated for the
next beta: Carbon's categorical grades are isoluminant, so a greyscale print
collapses every chart series to the same value. See
`docs/reports/chart-colors.md`.

**Goal, stated as a test:** a staff member who has branded LOTTO can brand FEED
without relearning anything. Workflow parity is the acceptance criterion, not a
nice-to-have.

---

## Which LOTTO document is the source

LOTTO solved this in two layers, a year apart, and it is easy to read the wrong
one:

- `WHITE_LABEL_BRANDING_PLAN.md` (LOTTO v1.19.0) — build-time, code-owned brand
  profiles selected by `NEXT_PUBLIC_LOTTO_BRAND`. Useful background; **not**
  what we are porting.
- `CONFIGURABLE_BRANDING_PLAN.md` (LOTTO v1.20.0) — the database-backed
  Appearance wizard a non-technical operator completes without touching source.
  **This is the port target.**

FEED already owns the UX idiom LOTTO's wizard uses. LOTTO deliberately built its
Appearance stepper on the pattern it inherited *from* FEED's AI Configuration
wizard. `packages/frontend/src/components/ai-configuration/shared/BaseAIConfigDialog.tsx`
is still that component. Building the Customization wizard on it produces parity
by construction rather than by imitation.

---

## Hard constraint, carried forward

**ONE DEPLOYMENT PER AGENCY. NOT MULTI-TENANCY.**

Each agency runs its own instance with its own database. There is no `tenantId`
column, no agency filter, no brand-switching in the request path. Each database
holds at most one active configuration. `AGENTS.md` opens with the
shared-whole-organization principle and marks it hard-won — the `ownerId`
partition torn out in ISSUES.md #31 was this same mistake at smaller scale, and
someone will propose the larger version in good faith unless this says
otherwise in plain terms.

---

## Architecture

### Brand resolution order (first match wins)

1. Active `BrandConfiguration` row in this deployment's database
2. Compiled William Temple House default

Any storage error, invalid payload, or derivation failure **falls back to the
compiled default** and surfaces the failure in Settings → Customization. A
broken saved appearance must never take down a public surface. Copied verbatim
from LOTTO, where it is the load-bearing safety contract.

### FEED has three colour systems, not one

| System | Location | Format today | Under configuration |
|---|---|---|---|
| App tokens | `packages/frontend/src/index.css` | 118 bare HSL triplets | Tailwind refs → HSL, then OKLCH at v1.7.5 |
| Charts | `packages/frontend/src/lib/colors.ts` | IBM Carbon hex | Carbon families ranked by hue distance |
| Print / PDF | `packages/backend/src/services/reports/*.ts` | hardcoded hex | Same token map, hex serializer |

The print palette (`#2964A3`, `#3b6ea5`, `#eef3f8` in `analytics-print.ts` and
`pdf.ts`) is deliberately William Temple House blue — a considered FEED choice,
not an oversight. It must stay brand-aligned under configuration, which means
the derivation output has to be portable beyond CSS.

**Therefore the derivation emits a structured `TokenMap`, never CSS text**, with
three serializers hanging off it. This is the same token-map intermediate
representation LOTTO built (for forward-compatibility with sparse overrides);
here it additionally unifies three colour systems.

```text
Brand colours + logo  →  snap to { accent, neutral } Tailwind families
                      →  role-to-stop map
                      →  TokenMap  (structured palette references)
                      →  ├─ HSL triplet serializer   (app CSS, v1.7.0)
                         ├─ OKLCH serializer         (app CSS, v1.7.5)
                         ├─ hex serializer           (PDF / print)
                         └─ Carbon family ranking    (charts)
```

### Colour: snap to Tailwind v4, do not derive

**Decision, 2026-08-27.** Brand colours snap to the nearest entry in Tailwind
v4's OKLCH palette (FEED ships 4.3.3) rather than being reproduced exactly and
used as the seed for arithmetic derivation.

The rationale is that brand alignment is reconstructing a colour *story*, not
matching a hex value. Perception does not track the maths closely enough for
exactness to pay for itself — see Hexcodle's data on how poorly people dial in a
colour by hand, and Keith Cirkel's "Too Much Color", which tests the
diminishing-returns hypothesis directly. What is lost in precision is repaid in
simplicity, and the simplicity turns out to be structural rather than cosmetic.

This is also the same move already accepted for charts. "Rank, don't generate"
against Carbon and "reproduce exactly" for brand hue cannot both be right.

**Measured against four real brand colours** (OKLab Euclidean distance,
`snap.mjs`, 2026-08-27):

| Brand colour | Actual (OKLCH) | Snaps to | Distance | Hue error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WTH blue `#186090` | 47.1% .103 243.5 | `sky-800` | 0.029 | 2.7° |
| WTH gold `#FFE066` | 91.0% .144 95.1 | `amber-200` | 0.028 | 0.6° |
| St. Johns teal `#33A478` | 64.4% .121 163.1 | `emerald-600` | 0.054 | 0.2° |
| St. Johns charcoal `#2D2D2D` | 29.7% .000 89.9 | `zinc-800` | 0.020 | n/a |

Hue lands within three degrees on every one. St. Johns is the loosest fit and
the error is lightness, not hue. Note it snaps to **emerald**, not **teal**,
despite the brand being named teal — the maths does not respect a colour's name,
so the wizard shows the operator the top three candidates rather than hiding the
choice.

#### Two constraints the measurement exposed

**1. Snapping must be role-aware.** Tailwind 4.3.3 carries 26 families: 17
chromatic and 9 neutral, the last four of which (`mauve`, `olive`, `mist`,
`taupe`) are lightly tinted. Snapped against the full set, St. Johns'
dead-neutral charcoal (chroma 0.000) lands on `olive-800` — a warm green cast
across every surface in the app. Brand accents snap within the chromatic pool;
surfaces and text snap within the neutral pool.

**2. Pick the family once, the stop per token.** Snapping each token
independently scatters a theme across families — card in `slate`, muted in
`mauve`, popover in `zinc` — destroying the internal coherence of the Tailwind
ramp, which is the entire reason to use it. Asking instead which *single*
neutral family best serves all seven of FEED's surface tokens:

| Family | Avg distance | Stop assignment |
|---|---|---|
| **slate** | 0.0204 | `900 950 800 500 · 50 100 300` |
| gray | 0.0224 | `900 950 800 500 · 50 100 300` |
| zinc | 0.0281 | `900 950 800 500 · 50 100 300` |
| neutral | 0.0320 | `900 950 800 500 · 50 100 300` |
| olive | 0.0448 | `900 950 900 500 · 50 100 300` |

`slate` wins for FEED, which is intuitively right — it is the blue-tinted
neutral and FEED's surfaces sit at hue 211–222.

**The stop assignment is identical for every family.** The stop is a property of
the token's *role*, not of the palette; only `olive`, the worst fit, deviates by
one. So the derivation is not OKLCH arithmetic at all — it is **two family
choices plus a fixed role-to-stop map**. A complete theme is roughly as complex
as `{ accent: "sky", neutral: "slate" }`.

#### Three consequences, all simplifications

- **Gamut clamping is unnecessary.** Every Tailwind palette entry is already
  in sRGB, so there is no out-of-gamut colour to clip and no risk of a brand
  shifting appearance across the v1.7.5 boundary.
- **The v1.7.5 migration shrinks.** Tokens stop being generated colour values
  and become references into a palette FEED already ships.
- **Contrast becomes provable rather than checked.** See below.

### Contrast: prove the space, don't validate the instance

17 chromatic × 9 neutral families is **153 possible themes** — with a fixed stop
map, that is the complete space, not a sample of it. Every one is contrast-
testable in a build-time test.

This is categorically stronger than LOTTO's guarantee. LOTTO derives freely, so
it validates each configuration as it is saved and auto-corrects failing derived
pairs at runtime; a brand nobody has tried is a brand nobody has verified. FEED
can instead assert that *every theme an operator can produce* has already
passed.

Where a combination fails, the fix is to adjust the stop map or exclude the
pairing in the wizard with a stated reason — decisions made once, by us, with
the whole space visible, rather than by an operator at save time facing an error.

**This resolves a live regression risk rather than merely flagging it.**
`packages/frontend/src/test/chart-colors.test.ts` currently reads `--card` out
of `index.css` and asserts every Carbon grade clears 4.5:1 against it. The
moment surfaces become configurable that test keeps passing — it is reading the
compiled default — while a real agency's saved surface could push chart series
below the floor. The replacement asserts across all 153 combinations: the same
test, given a domain instead of a value.

**Floors:** 4.5:1 for chart series and body text on surfaces; 3:1 for large text
and UI fills, per WCAG. Auto-correct only where *both* sides of a pair are
derived. Where an operator-typed colour is involved, name the failing pairing
and what would fix it — silently overriding a colour someone chose is worse than
reporting it. LOTTO's 2.5:1 emphasis floor is deliberately **not** imported: it
was reverse-engineered from two brands that failed 3:1, and FEED starts stricter.

### Charts: rank Carbon, never generate

FEED's chart palette is IBM Carbon — ten families, primary and secondary grades,
separate light and dark values, every one already verified at 4.5:1 against the
card surface. That is a real accessibility asset and generating colours
alongside it would undermine it.

Given the brand's accent hue, rank the ten Carbon families by hue distance and
assign series in that order. A teal-branded agency leads with Carbon teal and
cyan; a blue-branded one leads with blue. Every colour still comes from Carbon,
so every contrast guarantee survives; only which accessible colour appears first
changes.

Two guards:

- **Minimum hue separation between adjacent series.** Ranking by proximity to
  the brand naturally clusters similar hues, which is precisely what makes a
  multi-series line chart unreadable. Enforce a floor after ranking.
- **Status-encoded colours stay pinned.** Where red means danger and green means
  success, meaning outranks ordering.

### Delivery: a render-blocking stylesheet route

LOTTO injects theme CSS into its server-rendered Next.js layout, so first paint
carries the saved brand. FEED has no render step — `packages/frontend/index.html`
is a static build artifact served by nginx with `try_files`.

The fix is simpler than LOTTO's, not harder: **one render-blocking
`<link rel="stylesheet">` in `index.html` pointing at a backend-generated
route.** nginx already proxies `/api/`. A stylesheet in `<head>` blocks paint by
default, so there is no flash, no bootstrap script, and no client-side FOUC
workaround. Cacheable with an ETag.

### Assets: in the database

LOTTO stores uploaded assets on the filesystem, which is not durable on Vercel —
an open gap acknowledged in their own plan, whose answer is Vercel Blob storage.
FEED has no such constraint.

Storing logo and icon assets in the database means they ride the existing backup
and restore path for free, so a restored deployment comes back fully branded,
and it sidesteps the Pi's volume question entirely. Cap upload size and generate
derivatives on write — the 32GB card is a known constraint (see the build and
deploy memory note).

The upload contract preserves the source format where resolution matters. SVG
logos remain SVG after a structural sanitizer removes scripts, event handlers,
embedded media, animation, and every non-local reference. XML document types
are rejected before parsing; the delivery route adds `nosniff` and a sandboxed
CSP as defense in depth. PNGs are losslessly re-encoded at their original
dimensions. Raster logos below
576×160 and square marks below 512×512 produce a visible quality warning.
Only the fixed 64/192/512 app-mark derivatives are always PNG.

Uploads precede configuration saves, so abandoned wizard sessions can leave
unreferenced database rows. Data Management → Data provides an administrator
storage check and confirmed cleanup. It derives references from every saved
configuration and protects uploads less than one hour old so a concurrent open
wizard cannot lose its image.

### What stays code-owned

- All inventory, translation, shopping list, service, analytics, and import
  behaviour.
- **Protected operational semiotics**, absent from the schema entirely so a
  saved configuration cannot express the override: the four inventory status
  flags (`inStock`, `limited`, `clearance`, `outOfStock`) plus `destructive` and
  `success`. These mean the same thing at every agency and staff read them at
  speed.
- **Protected analytic semiotics** — the counting nouns. See terminology below.
- Component geometry, layout, fonts, and the three-state theme CSS model
  (`docs/frontend-services/theme-control.md`).

---

## Semantic terminology (ZEV Prism model)

FEED is built for Oregon food pantries. It is not a general inventory tool and
would not serve a clinic or a library well — so this is **not** about abstracting
the domain away. The real variation is *between pantries*: one says client,
another guest, neighbour, shopper or participant; one has a Social Services
department and another does not.

Measured surface: `pantry` appears ~50 times in non-test frontend source;
`Social Services` 11 times across source and docs.

Four of Prism's decisions transfer unchanged:

1. **Store singular and plural explicitly**, never auto-pluralize. English is
   irregular ("person" → "people"), and an i18n library is a poor trade for a
   handful of nouns.
2. **Placeholder templates**, not concatenation — `"Total {plural} served"`.
   Concatenated copy goes stilted the moment a configured term is longer than
   the word it replaced.
3. **Display layer only.** Prism's "Why Not Apply to Data Layer" is the
   important one: terms never touch the database, the API contract, or analytics
   logic.
4. **Soft-deactivate rather than delete.** This suits FEED better than it suited
   Prism — the domain is already revision-oriented and append-only throughout.

### Protected analytic semiotics

Just as inventory status colours are protected operational semiotics, **FEED's
counting nouns are protected analytic semiotics**: `household`, `visit`,
`person served`. These carry precise definitions that
`docs/reports/service-analytics-plan.md` and
`docs/reports/analytics-report-architecture.md` work hard to keep straight —
which record answers which question, and why two of them are never summed.
Letting an agency rename them would quietly dismantle that discipline. They stay
fixed, for exactly the same reason the status colours do.

How far configurable terminology goes beyond that is a judgement call exercised
as we go. The placeholder templating makes widening it later additive rather
than a migration.

---

## Settings, restructured

Tabs on the Analytics pattern (`packages/frontend/src/components/analytics/index.tsx`):

| Tab | Section | Scope | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General** | Operating Hours | Organization | All staff |
| **Appearance** | Theme | This device | All staff |
| **Appearance** | **Customization** | Organization | Administrators |

**Gate the Customization section, not the Appearance tab.** `/settings` is
staff-visible (`App.tsx` — it sits outside the `AdminRoute` guard), and
`AGENTS.md` is specific that the deliberate three-way light/dark/system choice
lives there; the header button is a two-state toggle where "follow this device"
is arrived at rather than offered. Hiding the tab would take System away from
every non-administrator.

"Customization" rather than "Appearance" for the section: it avoids
Appearance-inside-Appearance, and it is the more accurate word once the section
holds terminology as well as colour.

---

## Phases

Each phase is independently deployable. Two releases plus the migration, per the
roadmap's "deploy smaller, more often" — five phases held undeployed is exactly
the shape that produced two defects within an hour of the beta.21 deploy.

### Phase 0 — Snap, token map, and the contrast proof (v1.7.0)

**Post-review corrections, 2026-08-27.** Manual inspection after the beta
produced four changes to the design as planned:

- **The compiled William Temple House default is no longer derived.** It ships
  the hand-tuned token values, and the runtime stylesheet emits nothing until an
  appearance is configured. The fidelity gate had been reduced to a tautology
  (threshold 0.002 while `index.css` itself held the derived output, so
  derivation was measured against derivation); it is restored to 0.2 with its
  documented divergence list. Derivation's job is to get a *new* agency close
  from a logo, not to restate an identity already tuned by eye.
- **Deployment capabilities left the appearance payload.** A new
  `DeploymentSettings` singleton owns whether the public inventory feed is
  published, surfaced in Data Management for administrators. The
  appearance-scoped flag was unreachable whenever the compiled default was
  active, because that path stores no row.
- **Storage failures are translated before they reach a person.** Prisma's
  message embeds the invocation, a source excerpt, and absolute server paths;
  rendering it violated ASK and disclosed the server's layout.
- **A from-scratch appearance starts with a neutral placeholder mark**, not the
  St. Johns template logo.

**Complete in `v1.7.5-beta.1`.**

Role-aware snapping against the Tailwind 4.3.3 palette; the role-to-stop map;
the `TokenMap` with three serializers. Declare the protected families. Replace
the chart-contrast test with one asserting across all 153 family combinations.

**Gate:** re-derive today's William Temple House identity from brand inputs and
compare against `index.css`. If the pipeline cannot reproduce the theme we
already ship, it is not ready for anyone else's.

### Phase 1 — Persistence and delivery (v1.7.0)

**Complete in `v1.7.5-beta.1`.**

`BrandConfiguration` model on the existing singleton-plus-JSON precedent
(`LottoQueueIntegrationConfig`, `OperatingHoursRevision`), assets in the
database. Resolution order, fail-closed. Backend-generated stylesheet route with
an ETag, linked render-blocking from `index.html`. Brand context supplying
identity strings to React. Included in backup and restore.

**Gate:** activate a seeded template row and watch the whole app change identity
— no rebuild, no flash, charts included.

### Phase 2 — The Customization wizard (v1.7.0 ships here)

**Complete in `v1.7.5-beta.1`.**

Six steps on `BaseAIConfigDialog`: Start, Identity, Logos and icons, Colours,
Staff copy, Review. Publishing the public inventory is a deployment data-sharing
decision in Data Management, not an Appearance step. The Colours step
shows the snap and its top three alternates rather than hiding the choice.
Server-side dimension measurement and icon generation from one square mark. Live
preview including a real chart, in light and dark. Draft, activate, and a
session-scoped preview so an operator can walk the real app in a candidate
identity before committing.

**Gate:** a from-scratch run by someone who has used LOTTO's wizard, with no
instructions from us.

### Phase 3 — The surfaces that leave the building (v1.7.1)

**Complete in `v1.7.5-beta.1`.**

Report PDFs and CSVs take the print serializer instead of the hardcoded blues.
Email brand derived from the same config, as LOTTO's `auth-email-brand.ts` does.
Public inventory organization fields. Analytics provenance copy that currently
names the agency inline.

**Gate:** a generated funder PDF and a magic-link email rendered under a
non-default brand — and the PDF diffed against current output to confirm nothing
regressed for William Temple House.

### Phase 4 — Semantic terminology and the capstone (v1.7.1 ships here)

**Complete in `v1.7.5-beta.1`.**

Prism's model implemented: singular/plural pairs, placeholder templates, derived
phrase book, context provider, soft deactivation, display layer only. Then the
brand-swap test.

**Gate — the capstone.** Configure FEED to look on-brand for St. Johns Food
Share using only the wizard, and back again. LOTTO's St. Johns identity is
hand-tuned and production-validated, so success is not a matter of taste: it is
a side-by-side review at mobile and desktop widths in light and dark. "Not
exactly like the other" is acceptable; off-brand is not. Status colours must be
identical in both directions.

### Phase 5 — OKLCH migration (v1.7.5)

**Complete in `v1.7.5-beta.1`.** App-shell gradients now derive from semantic
brand tokens as well, so a runtime identity does not retain a hard-coded WTH
blue atmosphere behind rebranded content.

Swap the app serializer, stop wrapping tokens in `hsl()` inside `@theme inline`,
convert the alpha-form sites catalogued during v1.7.0, and adopt the Tailwind
palette as the authored baseline throughout.

**Watch for:** `hsl(var(--background) / 0.40)` and its siblings in the app-shell
atmosphere read the raw triplet directly and break on migration day. Catalogue
them in v1.7.0 rather than discovering them here.

**Gate:** identical brand inputs produce visually identical output across the
boundary — the Phase 0 fidelity comparison, run twice.

## Decisions and reasoning

Recorded so the reasoning survives, not just the outcome. Settled 2026-08-27.

| # | Decision | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | General + Appearance tabs; gate the **Customization section**, not the tab | Gating the tab would take the three-state theme picker from all non-administrators |
| D2 | Snap to Tailwind v4, role-aware, one family per role plus a fixed stop map | Precision traded for simplicity, a provable contrast space, and no gamut clamping |
| D3 | Rank Carbon by hue distance; never generate chart colours | Preserves an existing WCAG-verified palette; brand alignment costs no accessibility |
| D4 | Protect four status flags plus destructive and success | Operational semiotics staff read at speed; identical at every agency |
| D5 | Assets in the database | Rides existing backup/restore; LOTTO's Vercel Blob constraint does not apply |
| D6 | Email and PDF in scope (Phase 3); fonts out | They reach funders and clients; PDF font embedding has documented traps here |
| D7 | Terminology as far as judgement requires, on Prism's model | FEED stays a food-pantry tool; this is variation between pantries |
| D8 | William Temple House stays the compiled default | Pi deploy is a no-op on merge; adopters inherit something proven at a real agency |
| D9 | Sparse-override pipeline yes, Advanced UI no | Basic must prove itself against a real second agency first |
| D10 | 4.5:1 body and charts, 3:1 large text and UI fills | FEED starts stricter than LOTTO; do not import a floor reverse-engineered from two brands |
| D11 | v1.7.0 at Phase 2, v1.7.1 at Phase 4, v1.7.5 for the migration | Five phases held undeployed is the shape that hid defects before |

---

## Deviation from the v1.6→v2.0 roadmap

That roadmap slots white-label at v2.0, paired with Prisma 7, and describes
brand configuration as "Mechanical."

- **Sequencing.** Moved to v1.7.0 at the user's direction. This displaces
  Shopping List grid layouts and the Builder UX rework, which is clean: those
  two are coupled to *each other* (the roadmap explicitly says do grids first)
  and neither is coupled to branding. They shift down intact.
- **"Mechanical" is wrong.** The design ports; the delivery is a rewrite. FEED
  has no SSR, no PWA manifest, three colour systems rather than one, and an
  HSL-triplet token vocabulary where LOTTO is OKLCH-native. Calling it
  mechanical sets the estimate up to be wrong.
- **Prisma 6 → 7 stays separate**, per the roadmap's own instruction to split
  it from the surface change so a failure has one candidate cause.
- **Deployment capability configuration** — which import sources exist,
  generalized quirk rules, the 264-person Thanksgiving prompt — is explicitly
  **out of scope**. It is the harder design problem, it is not branding, and its
  precedent is the administrator-configurable Service Metrics FEED already has.
  Bundling it here is how v1.7.0 slips.
